oq4e_mtp.status: NOT_AVAILABLE_LOCALLY; no local DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-oQ4e-mtp checkpoint found under /Volumes, ~/.cache/mlx-lm, or ~/.omlx

benchmark_settings.main_stock_runs: Code/Python repeated prompt truncated to context; BatchGenerator direct; 128 generated tokens except release-official-off-4k used 32 tokens as a quick OFF check; temperature=1.0 categorical unless noted; top_p=1; top_k=0; prefix cache disabled; Engram SSD; sequential runs; model load excluded from decode tok/s
deviations: The published oQ4e-mtp checkpoint was not locally available, so dev2 oQ4e reproduction was not run.
No 16K/32K expansion was needed after 4K and 64K stock official runs identified the dominant cause.
Warm-up was omitted in the recorded per-run files; the same loaded model was measured after prefill, and decode-only throughput is reported.

priming_findings.upstream_contract: When MTP is active, DeepSeek V4.1 __call__ asks _forward for DSpark target hidden during ordinary prompt prefill, capture_prompt appends selected target-layer hidden into DSparkContextCache and records expected_target_offset, and take_primed transfers those caches into the generation loop after the first main token.
priming_findings.m25_gap: M25 intentionally ran ds41f DENSE_P0_P7 with MTP OFF during P7 and supplied only the terminal token to upstream BatchGenerator. The host prime context was absent at generation start in M25 artifacts.
priming_findings.effect: At comparable OFF speed (~19.6-20 tok/s), restoring stock full prompt priming on the official checkpoint raised MTP to 41.5-42.7 tok/s with ~94.5% checked-draft acceptance, versus 20.0-24.7 tok/s and 48-71% in M25 terminal-only runs. This directly isolates missing prompt priming as the dominant measured cause.

checkpoint_findings.oq4e_status: Not reproduced because the oQ4e-mtp checkpoint was unavailable locally.
checkpoint_findings.inference_from_available_data: Checkpoint representation is not required to exceed the published 34-36 tok/s: the official checkpoint with stock full prompt priming reached 41-44 tok/s on this machine. Therefore oQ4e cannot be the dominant explanation of why M25 was slow, although it may explain differences between the published 34-36 tok/s and this official-checkpoint stock diagnostic.

revision_findings.dev2_vs_release_official_4k: No regression found in the measured path. dev2 official MTP 43.99 tok/s vs release official MTP 42.68 tok/s; dev2 OFF 20.03 vs release OFF 19.94. The small difference is not large enough to explain M25.
revision_findings.dev2_limitations: The preserved dev2 checkout is dirty in encoding.py/processing.py plus an untracked test; those files are not the measured DSpark/MTP core, and the run is diagnostic-only.

workload_sampling_findings.release_4k_categorical_vs_greedy: Stock full-primed greedy still reached 39.96 tok/s and 90.9% acceptance, close to categorical 42.68 tok/s and far above M25. Sampling/workload contributes but is secondary to priming.
workload_sampling_findings.m25_synthetic: M25's deterministic synthetic fixture had lower acceptance under terminal-only priming, especially at 200K. The fixture likely amplified the priming problem but does not explain it alone.

dominant_attribution: P7 / missing full DSpark prompt priming is dominant for the large gap. OFF speed was already equivalent; native full prompt priming on the same official checkpoint and release oMLX produces large speculative gains.
decision: A. MTP remains worth pursuing, but production remains MTP OFF and the M25 committed-idle/no-replay lifecycle rejection is unchanged. The next MTP milestone should address the no-replay committed-idle transition only after preserving/restoring the upstream DSpark prompt-priming state contract.
